reason: Attacked hardest of the four, because the verifier changed the wording, and the correction survives. I re-ran the probe myself: a HathiTrust full text phrase search on the whole shipped sentence, In every town and every village and every mud hut in the world there is always a man who loves children and who will fight to make a good world for them, returns 29 volumes, and the second hit is Watch on the Rhine, a play in three acts / by Lillian Hellman (1941), the Random House first printing that the citation names. Shortening the probe raises the count as a real phrase search should (the same sentence minus its opening clause gives 44, every mud hut in the world alone gives 69), and a control probe on another line with one leading word swapped returns No results match your search, so the index is word-exact and not ignoring short words. The three ands are therefore in the printed play and the comma-only form that travels online is not the play's. Attribution: Hellman, correct, and nothing on the misattribution list touches it. Speaker and locator: Kurt Muller's farewell to Joshua, Babette and Bodo comes in Act Three, after the Act Two confrontation with Teck, which matches the structure of the play and the research starter the verifier cites. Scope: a stage play, Random House 1941, well before 1999; the 1943 film keeps the speech but the citation is to the play. shipped.js: no shipped or near match, Lillian Hellman at 0 of 3, not banned; she also helps the month's floor of eight women. Form: source line 111 characters, no dash, speaker in parentheses, tag Drama. Publishable: the killing is offstage and outside the quotation. Two things the evidence cannot carry and the note should say plainly: a phrase search is blind to punctuation, so whether the play prints a comma after in the world is not established by it, and the Act Three placement rests on a reference summary rather than on the page itself.
